name: codex
title: Codex / GPT cross-vendor interface
summary: Adds the OpenAI-backed half of the harness: the Sol reviewer as the default cross-family reviewer for Claude-authored campaign work through the Codex CLI, an exceptional-order-only Sol executor through the same CLI, and the two-architect /cross-compare-plan session (independent drafts, cross-critique, blind synthesis) whose GPT lane (Sol, high effort) runs read-only through the same CLI.

bin: codex (Codex CLI) — for reviewer-codex, executor-codex-heavy, and the cross-compare architect lane
env: OPENAI_API_KEY or `codex login` — review, execution, and cross-compare

notes: reviewer-codex is the default independent reviewer for Claude-authored campaign work; Codex-authored work goes to fresh-context Opus review instead. There is no reviewEngine switch.

executor-codex-heavy is exceptional-only: a problem with concrete prior evidence that Anthropic models struggled on it, a Director routing decision made at PLAN time — never routine work. The Claude executors remain the default path.

Config keys (.claude/orchestra.json under "codex"): reviewModel (default gpt-5.6-sol), reviewTimeoutMs (default 1800000), execHeavyModel (default gpt-5.6-sol), execHeavyEffort (default high), crossplanModel (default gpt-5.6-sol), crossplanEffort (default high).

Windows: codex-command-runner.exe, codex-resources AND codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe must sit DIRECTLY beside codex.exe. Codex resolves the sandbox helper by name, so a copy one directory down (inside codex-resources\) is never found — the sandbox is never set up and BOTH lanes (review and execution) return nothing while looking healthy. The self-check below finds that state and repairs it where it can.
Without this pack the harness still gets full fresh-context Opus review and Claude execution; it just has no cross-vendor option.
